clues: This town is in the Northern Cape province of South Africa. It sits on the banks of the Orange River.
The land is very dry, but the soil near the river is rich and good for crops. Fruit grows there in fields that get extra water.
It was first a mission station, in eighteen seventy one. Reverend Christiaan Schröder was the man who ran it.
A museum here holds a statue of a donkey. It thanks the hard work these animals did to help build up this dry region long ago.
This place is best known for fine grapes, raisins, and wines. They grow on the rich flood plains of the Orange River.
